title: Optional string fields sent as null

source.clause: §5.1.1, §5.2.1; Annex A (Content typed as a union including null, MessageType as a string)
source.note: composed: the counterpart of 33-content-null-text. `MessageType` and `Label` are optional and typed as strings, so a null there carries nothing the standard could interpret and is read as an absence rather than refused.

notes: The asymmetry with `content: null` is Annex A's: the schema types `Content` as a union that includes null and `MessageType` as a string, so a null content is a value the message carries and a null message type is a field it does not. A *required* string field sent as null is a missing field, not an absence to tolerate — case 20 pins that for `subformat`.
